title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government is responding to the 2020 Committee report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining how it plans to strengthen rules and oversight. It emphasizes transparency, accountability, and safety for AI systems while supporting innovation.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual sets out how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in England’s qualification tests and assessments, aiming to keep them fair, secure, and transparent. The policy was drafted after a joint request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how using copyrighted works affects the training and operation of AI systems, identifying potential legal, ethical, and practical issues. It also offers recommendations for policymakers and industry stakeholders to manage copyright concerns while fostering AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government outlines its response to the Lords report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency”, explaining how it plans to address AI’s risks and benefits. It details policy measures aimed at fostering innovation while ensuring safety, transparency and fairness in the UK’s AI landscape.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document outlines the terms of reference for a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards and includes FAQs to explain its scope and objectives. It serves as a guide for stakeholders to understand the committee’s role, responsibilities, and the process for assessing AI’s impact on public standards.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of Artificial Intelligence. In its submission, the organization shares its viewpoints and proposes recommendations for how AI should be regulated and managed.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy looks at how artificial intelligence changes the rules that govern medical products and explains how to put the AI White Paper’s principles into practice. It aims to keep AI‑enabled medical devices safe, transparent, and accountable while fitting them into existing regulatory frameworks.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our defence organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential in AI for its size. It outlines how we will develop, adopt, and govern AI technologies to support national security and operational excellence.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to harness AI benefits while mitigating risks. It details strategies for innovation, safety, regulation, and workforce development to support a safer, more efficient, and sustainable transport system.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyright‑protected works are used to train AI models, highlighting progress and challenges under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines current practices, legal interpretations, and recommendations for balancing innovation with copyright protection.
